title: Node.js Web Development
description: Beginner-to-advanced Node.js runtime reference covering modules, packages, event loop, async design, files, streams, HTTP, processes, workers, testing, diagnostics, security, and production operation.

sections.title: Runtime, Modules & Packages
sections.description: Choose a supported runtime and make module/package boundaries explicit.

subtopics.title: Release Lines & API Stability
subtopics.description: Production applications should use an Active or Maintenance LTS release. Check each API's stability marker before depending on experimental behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
node --version
node --help
node --run test
node --watch src/server.js
node --env-file=.env src/server.js

callouts.title: Pin the Runtime
callouts.text: Declare engines and pin CI/container/runtime versions. Even-numbered release 24 is LTS in July 2026; 26 is Current and should not be assumed production LTS yet.

subtopics.title: ES Modules & CommonJS
subtopics.description: ESM uses import/export and URL-based resolution; CommonJS uses require/module.exports. Select with package.json type and file extensions.

tabs.label: ESM
CommonJS

callouts.title: Do Not Mix Mental Models
callouts.text: __dirname, require cache, extension resolution, top-level await, and interop differ. Publish explicit exports and test both import/require entry points if supporting both.

subtopics.title: package.json, Exports & Lockfiles
subtopics.description: Define scripts, engine support, entry points, dependency types, and a public export map; commit one package-manager lockfile.

callouts.title: Dependencies Have Meaning
callouts.text: Runtime imports belong in dependencies; build/test tools in devDependencies; peerDependencies express a host-provided compatibility contract for plugins/libraries.

sections.title: Event Loop & Asynchronous Design
sections.description: Keep the event-loop thread responsive and make cancellation/failure explicit.

subtopics.title: Event Loop, Microtasks & Blocking
subtopics.description: JavaScript callbacks run on the event-loop thread. I/O can be concurrent through the OS/libuv pool, but CPU-heavy JavaScript blocks every request in that process.

codeBlocks.code:
Current callback → process.nextTick queue → Promise microtasks → event-loop phases
Timers: setTimeout/setInterval
Poll: I/O callbacks
Check: setImmediate
Close callbacks

Avoid long synchronous JSON, crypto, compression, regex, loops, and sync fs on request paths.

callouts.title: Microtask Starvation
callouts.text: Recursive process.nextTick or Promise scheduling can starve I/O. Yield intentionally and move sustained CPU work to worker threads or another service.

subtopics.title: Promises, async/await & Error Boundaries
subtopics.description: Await promises, return them to callers, and catch failures at a layer that can add context or produce an appropriate response.

callouts.title: Unhandled Rejections Are Bugs
callouts.text: Do not fire-and-forget promises without an owner and rejection handler. Crash/restart on unknown corrupted process state; do not continue blindly after uncaught failures.

subtopics.title: AbortSignal, Timeouts & Bounded Concurrency
subtopics.description: Propagate AbortSignal through supported APIs and limit concurrent work to protect memory, connections, and upstreams.

callouts.title: Promise.all Is Unbounded
callouts.text: Mapping thousands of records into Promise.all starts them immediately. Use a pool/queue and define partial failure, cancellation, and retry policy.

sections.title: Files, Buffers & Streams
sections.description: Choose whole-value or streaming APIs based on size and flow control.

subtopics.title: Paths, URLs & File APIs
subtopics.description: Use node:path for filesystem paths and URL for URLs/ESM-relative resources. Prefer promise APIs and atomic replacement for critical writes.

callouts.title: Validate User Paths
callouts.text: Resolve against an allowed root and verify containment; reject traversal and symlink surprises. Never concatenate untrusted paths into shell commands.

subtopics.title: Buffer, Text Encoding & Binary Data
subtopics.description: Buffer is a byte sequence. Decode/encode with explicit character encodings and distinguish byte length from JavaScript string length.

callouts.title: Uninitialized Memory
callouts.text: allocUnsafe may contain prior memory. Use only when every byte is overwritten before exposure; use alloc for security-sensitive or partial writes.

subtopics.title: Streams, pipeline & Backpressure
subtopics.description: Streams process large data incrementally. pipeline connects stages, propagates errors, and cleans up; respect write() false/drain for manual producers.

callouts.title: Do Not Buffer Unbounded Inputs
callouts.text: readFile, request body concatenation, and Response.text load everything into memory. Enforce size limits and stream uploads/downloads where appropriate.

sections.title: HTTP, Networking & Services
sections.description: Define request limits, response contracts, timeouts, and graceful connection behavior.

subtopics.title: HTTP Server Fundamentals
subtopics.description: The built-in HTTP server is low-level: parse URLs, route methods, stream bodies, set headers/status, and handle errors explicitly.

callouts.title: Set Defensive Limits
callouts.text: Configure header, body, request, idle, and upstream timeouts. Validate method/content type/input and avoid reflecting unsanitized values into headers or HTML.

subtopics.title: fetch, URL & Outbound Requests
subtopics.description: Use WHATWG URL to construct requests, AbortSignal for deadlines, explicit status checks, and bounded retries only for safe operations.

callouts.title: SSRF Boundary
callouts.text: Do not fetch arbitrary user-provided URLs. Allowlist schemes/hosts, protect private networks and redirects, and resolve DNS-rebinding concerns in the deployment layer.

subtopics.title: EventEmitter & Async Context
subtopics.description: EventEmitter dispatches synchronously in registration order. AsyncLocalStorage propagates request-scoped context through supported async operations.

callouts.title: Always Handle error Events
callouts.text: An EventEmitter error event without a listener throws. Define listener cleanup/lifetime and avoid turning a global event bus into invisible control flow.

sections.title: Processes, Workers & Lifecycle
sections.description: Use the right isolation boundary and shut down predictably.

subtopics.title: process, Environment & Signals
subtopics.description: Read environment at startup, validate into typed configuration, and handle termination signals by stopping new work and draining owned resources.

callouts.title: Do Not Call process.exit During Drain
callouts.text: Immediate exit can truncate logs and pending writes. Set exitCode and let handles drain, with an external or bounded forced-shutdown deadline.

subtopics.title: Worker Threads & Child Processes
subtopics.description: Worker threads parallelize CPU-heavy JavaScript with message/shared memory. Child processes isolate programs and are required for external commands.

table.title: Node.js Concurrency and Isolation Tools
rows: Small shell commands with bounded output
Use multiple CPU cores for a network service

callouts.title: Use execFile/spawn Without a Shell
callouts.text: Never interpolate untrusted input into exec command strings. Pass executable and argument arrays, restrict allowed commands, and handle stdout/stderr backpressure and exit codes.

subtopics.title: Timers, Handles & Resource Ownership
subtopics.description: Clear timers/listeners, close sockets/files, unref optional background timers, and expose explicit start/close lifecycle for long-lived services.

callouts.title: Open Handles Explain Hanging Tests
callouts.text: Servers, intervals, sockets, workers, and database pools keep the event loop alive. Make lifecycle explicit and close them in test cleanup.

sections.title: Testing, Diagnostics & Performance
sections.description: Use built-in observability and profile the correct bottleneck.

subtopics.title: node:test, Assertions & Mocking
subtopics.description: The stable built-in test runner supports suites, hooks, mocking, snapshots, coverage, and concurrency controls.

callouts.title: Control Time and I/O
callouts.text: Inject clocks, clients, and randomness; use temporary directories and local fake servers. Avoid live network and shared ports in unit tests.

subtopics.title: Inspector, Reports & Observability
subtopics.description: Use structured logs, metrics, traces, diagnostic reports, heap/CPU profiles, and event-loop delay/utilization measurements.

codeBlocks.code:
node --inspect src/server.js
node --cpu-prof src/server.js
node --heap-prof src/server.js
node --report-on-fatalerror src/server.js
node --trace-warnings src/server.js

callouts.title: Protect Diagnostic Endpoints
callouts.text: Inspector, heap snapshots, reports, environment, and stack traces can expose secrets and enable control. Never publish them unauthenticated.

subtopics.title: Event-Loop Latency, Memory & Profiling
subtopics.description: Measure throughput and tail latency under realistic load. Distinguish CPU saturation, I/O wait, garbage collection, memory retention, and downstream bottlenecks.

callouts.title: Streams Do Not Guarantee Low Memory
callouts.text: Ignoring backpressure, retaining chunks/listeners, or accumulating results still grows memory. Profile heap retainers rather than guessing.

sections.title: Security & Production Checklist
sections.description: Treat dependencies, inputs, privileges, resources, and runtime lifecycle as security boundaries.

subtopics.title: Input, Dependency & Runtime Security
subtopics.description: Validate inputs, encode for output context, use parameterized queries, pin dependencies, minimize permissions, and keep supported runtime releases patched.

codeBlocks.code:
Reject unknown/oversized fields and ambiguous content types
Use parameterized SQL; never construct commands from input
Allowlist redirect/URL targets and filesystem roots
Keep secrets out of source, logs, client bundles, and image layers
Commit lockfiles; review install scripts and supply-chain changes
Run as non-root with least filesystem/network capability
Set rate, body, header, connection, and execution limits

callouts.title: The Permission Model Is Defense in Depth
callouts.text: Node permission flags can reduce accidental access but do not replace OS/container isolation, dependency review, and application authorization.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Review support, ownership, bounded resources, observability, and graceful failure before deployment.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Supported LTS runtime is pinned across CI and production
□ ESM/CJS and package exports are intentional
□ Every promise, timer, listener, stream, worker, and socket has an owner
□ CPU-heavy work cannot block request event loops
□ Concurrency, bodies, queues, and retries are bounded
□ AbortSignal/timeouts propagate to downstream work
□ Streams use pipeline and respect backpressure
□ Inputs, paths, URLs, queries, and commands are validated
□ Errors add context without leaking secrets
□ SIGTERM drains traffic and closes dependencies
□ Health endpoints distinguish liveness/readiness
□ Logs, metrics, traces, event-loop delay, memory, and profiles are available
□ Tests clean all open handles and avoid live dependencies
